name: AI Foundational Concepts
definition: Ability to explain in age-appropriate terms how AI and machine-learning systems take in data, learn patterns, make predictions, and where the limits of machine intelligence lie.
uncertainty: Strong and broad evidence that AI/ML concepts are learnable across ages 6-18; age-specific progressions and durable transfer still need more longitudinal study.

name: Everyday AI Recognition
definition: Ability to recognize where AI and algorithms operate in everyday tools - search, recommendations, voice assistants, smart devices - and to question how they shape what we see and do.
uncertainty: Good empirical support that children can recognize and question everyday AI; evidence concentrates on informal and early-years settings and should be extended across secondary schooling.

name: Generative AI Literacy
definition: Ability to use generative AI tools effectively while understanding how they produce content, verifying their outputs, protecting personal data, and recognizing bias and limits.
uncertainty: Policy guidance is clear and recent, but classroom evidence on teaching generative AI use to ages 13-18 is still early and fast-moving.
